question:
Donna has $n$ boxes of doughnuts. Each box contains $13$ doughnuts.

After eating one doughnut, Donna is able to rearrange the remaining doughnuts into bags so that each bag contains $9$ doughnuts, and none are left over. What is the smallest possible value of $n$?
solution:
After Donna eats one doughnut, \(13n-1\) remain. To fill bags of 9 with none left over, she needs \(13n\equiv1\pmod 9\). Since \(13\equiv4\pmod 9\), this is \(4n\equiv1\pmod 9\). Multiply by 7: because \(7\cdot4=28\equiv1\pmod 9\), we get \(n\equiv7\pmod 9\). The smallest positive integer in that class is 7, and it leaves \(13\cdot7-1=90\) doughnuts for 10 bags.
Final answer: 7
